headline_marked: BTV's [[VAT exemption for World Cup broadcasting rights]] granted
headline: BTV's VAT exemption for World Cup broadcasting rights granted
summary: The National Board of Revenue has waived VAT on the 73 crore BDT cost of acquiring broadcasting rights for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
details: The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has granted a VAT exemption for Bangladesh Television (BTV) to purchase the broadcasting rights for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
BTV spent 73 crore BDT to acquire the 'all media rights' for the tournament, which is 25 crore BDT less than the cost of the previous tournament.
The Internal Resources Division (IRD) issued the order on July 2, stating that the exemption applies specifically to the purchase of these rights from FIFA.
To receive the benefit, BTV must follow four conditions, including notifying the relevant VAT commissionerate within 10 days of payment.
The exemption does not apply to sub-licensing agencies or any other services procured within Bangladesh.
The decision was approved by the government's procurement committee in a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on June 7.

The Internal Resources Division (IRD) issued the order on July 2, stating that the exemption applies specifically to the purchase of these rights from FIFA.

To receive the benefit, BTV must follow four conditions, including notifying the relevant VAT commissionerate within 10 days of payment.

The exemption does not apply to sub-licensing agencies or any other services procured within Bangladesh.

The decision was approved by the government's procurement committee in a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on June 7.

headline_marked: Winds of 315kph: [[Super Typhoon Bavi nears US Pacific islands]]
headline: Winds of 315kph: Super Typhoon Bavi nears US Pacific islands
summary: Residents of Guam and the Northern Marianas are evacuating as a Category 5-equivalent storm brings catastrophic damage warnings and 35-foot waves.
details: Super Typhoon Bavi is projected to hit US Pacific territories, including Guam and the Northern Marianas, with winds of 260 kph and gusts up to 315 kph, equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane.
The National Weather Service (NWS) has warned of 'catastrophic' damage near the storm's center, along with significant flooding from torrential rains and coastal inundation.
Projected waves of up to 35 feet—the height of a 10-storey building—are expected to create extremely dangerous conditions at sea.
In Guam, five evacuation centers in schools have been opened with a capacity of 1,900 people, as residents board up windows and seek shelter.
FEMA teams are on the ground with 1.1 million liters of water, 1.2 million meals, and 90 generators to support the affected population.
The region has been hit by several massive storms recently, including Super Typhoon Sinlaku in April and Typhoon Mawar in 2023, which caused widespread power and water outages.
Experts link the intensification of such tropical storms to record-breaking ocean temperatures and the emergence of a strong El Nino phenomenon in the tropical Pacific.
caption:
